deep.reconstruction:
This page continues p.20 (archive p.63). There Grothendieck had introduced the topological Teichmüller groupoids S T^±_top (surfaces of type (g,ν), oriented or not, with boundary circles, and the gluing and 'bouclage' operations). He then asked for a further structure: the fundamental groupoids Π_1(X,R), with a set R ≠ ∅ of base points (on the boundary). These should depend functorially on (X,R), commute with the gluing operations and be compatible with coverings X'→X. He wanted this realised as a strict functor from the Teichmüller groupoid (or a discrete or rigidified version, 'D') to a category of groupoids. On p.20 he had already warned that even for S T_{0,3} (pants) the question is non-trivial and perhaps too ambitious.

This page gives the reason. Such a strict, functorial realisation would require a 'model' of the topological Teichmüller groupoid big enough to contain, up to isomorphism, ALL curves (surfaces). He remarks 'ça fait un peu gros!', i.e. this is a size/strictification problem: one cannot naively take all surfaces as objects and get strict functoriality of Π_1.

He then retreats to a more modest goal. 'Without too much trouble' (or, on the alternative reading, 'at least in small dimensions'), one should be able to obtain the desired models for the discrete version S T D^±_top, models of the Π_1(X,R), and their functorial dependence on (X,R). In modern terms he wants a strictified model of the 'Teichmüller tower' (a modular-operad-like structure on surfaces with boundary) acting compatibly on fundamental groupoids with boundary base points. This is the topological prerequisite for an outer Galois / GT-type action on the tower of profinite fundamental groupoids.

The next page ('Découpage de cartes en pantalons généralisés') shows the intended route: build the models combinatorially from (generalised) pants decompositions of maps (cartes), i.e. from the building blocks of genus 0 with 3 (or few) boundary components. This is the 'Lego' philosophy later made explicit in the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error. The text is a heuristic remark (a size/strictification worry) rather than a claim. The worry is legitimate but avoidable by choosing a small skeleton, e.g. a standard surface for each type (g,ν) with chosen boundary parametrisations. This is essentially how later 'Lego' and surface-operad models proceed, so 'ça fait un peu gros' is a convenience issue rather than an obstruction.

ideas.what: Functorial dependence of fundamental groupoids Π_1(X,R), with base points in boundary set R, on (X,R), compatible with gluing of surfaces along boundary circles.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid on a set of base points with groupoid van Kampen; action of the mapping class groupoid / Teichmüller tower on fundamental groupoids of surfaces (tangential base points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (groupoid van Kampen, 1967); Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (1984), for the Teichmüller tower; later Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3 on the Teichmüller tower and fundamental groupoids with several base points (in loose form)

ideas.what: Need for a strict 'model' of the topological Teichmüller groupoid; a model containing all curves is too big, so one should use smaller models (the discrete version S T D^±) built from pants-type pieces.
ideas.modern_name: Strictification / skeleton of the modular operad of surfaces; Lego–Teichmüller game; surface operads
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in the Esquisse's 'jeu de Lego-Teichmüller'; the explicit size/strictification remark appears unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets as a goal a strictly functorial model of fundamental groupoids Π_1(X,R) over the (discrete) topological Teichmüller groupoid, compatible with gluing, coverings and orientation reversal (±). He flags the size problem and does not carry it out on this page.
missed.quote: elles exigerait d'avoir un "modèle" pour S T^±_top qui soit assez gros pour contenir ... toutes les courbes — ça fait un peu gros!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Strict operadic models of surfaces acting on free groupoids exist in the literature (parenthesised braids, surface operads, Lego–Teichmüller). However, the non-oriented (±) version with arbitrary base-point sets R and covering functoriality is less systematically treated. It is a mild open-ended thread rather than a missed result.

deep.surprise_reason: A candid working remark about the size/strictification problem for functorial models of fundamental groupoids over the Teichmüller tower. The ideas largely resurface in the Esquisse and in later Lego–Teichmüller and operadic work; there is no new finished result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the symbol is S𝒯^±_{top} (with an S prefix, as on the previous page), not \widehat{\mathcal{T}}^±_{top}. Similarly, on line 8 it is S𝒯D^±_{top}.
Line 3, the parenthetical, is barely legible: possibly '(comme un objet ...)' or '(à isomorphisme près ...)'; leave as [?].

The line after 'Mais quand même on doit pouvoir' plausibly reads 'sans trop de mal' (handwriting 'ss trop d. mal') rather than 'en tout cas en petites dimensions'. The following words ('... dans le(s) ...', 'fonction/foulée') are uncertain.
'des {+modèles des+} Π_1(X,R)': the inserted 'modèles des' is written above, with a brace over Π_1(X,R); Π_1 may carry no hat.
'feuilleté[?]' is doubtful; the word looks more like 'foulée' or 'fonction', unsure.
